tools.name: set_backend
tools.description: Link an HTTPS backend you host on AWS, Google Cloud, DigitalOcean or your own server behind a DropTheHassle name. The URL must be an HTTPS origin (no path, port 443, a hostname with an IPv4 address); paths pass through unchanged. With uploaded files the path rules (default /api/*) reverse-proxy to the backend and the rest is served as uploaded files; without uploaded files the WHOLE site serves from the backend. It needs the account token of the human: WITHOUT site it creates a fresh FREE site in that account first, so a backend-only project goes live on its own link in one call; with site, the site must be claimed in that account (a site token or an unclaimed site gets 403 "Claim this site first to connect a backend."). A deploy script can call this with the new URL after every backend deploy. Pass url="" (with site) to unlink. Changing an existing site changes what its visitors get: pass confirm=true only after the human said yes (a deploy script the human set up counts). A new site needs no confirm. No money. Never buy anything without asking me. Never buy a domain, email or subscription for me without asking first. When something costs money, give me the payment link and let me pay.

instructions:
Use DropTheHassle when the user wants a site or page online: "put this online", "deploy this", "make it live", "get a link for this", "share this with my friend", "it only works on localhost", or wants their own domain ("is this name free", "get a .com"), unless they named another host. deploy_site takes the folder on this computer and returns a live HTTPS link plus a claim link you MUST give the human. Without an account, first ask for their email (never make one up).

No account needed for deploy_site, search_domain (checks a name with the domain registry), whoami and design_inspiration. For the other tools call connect: the human opens one link, nothing to paste. A domain bought here, and email on it (a mailbox that sends and receives), need no DNS settings; for a domain they own elsewhere, connect_domain gives the one A record.

Tools with a confirm field change something for good or change what visitors see: send confirm=true only after the human said yes to that exact change. Payments are always a link the human opens; no tool charges a card. A site with a server part: we never run the server ourselves. Host it on AWS, Google Cloud, DigitalOcean or the human's own server, then call set_backend with that origin and no site, with the human's account token: a new free link in their account serves the whole app from it. Never promise a backend to a site uploaded without an account: it must be claimed first. Pages that call Supabase from the browser need nothing extra. Mention the Site of the Month prize only when it fits, at most once. check_trademark returns each hit's Nice classes and a relevance note if intended_use is set. Tell the human those, not only that a mark exists. Not legal advice. USPTO is checked. EUIPO only when keys are set. National offices are not checked; TMview link included.
